subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For Darwin gateway exec, should matched allowlist commands that contain shell syntax auto-execute only after OpenClaw can build an enforceable command plan, or should plan-miss prompting remain an intentional documented limitation?
rationale: This is an exec approval security boundary: restoring the documented automation improves production workflows, but bypassing the plan-miss gate without a safe plan could execute shell behavior that was not actually pinned by the allowlist.

options.title: Fix enforceable Darwin shapes
options.body: Implement safe plan construction for deterministic tilde and simple shell-shaped commands, keep prompt behavior for genuinely unenforceable plans, and add focused regression coverage.

options.title: Document the limitation
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed prompting behavior and update exec approval docs and warning text so operators can convert automated commands to argv-clean absolute paths.

options.title: Broaden raw allowlist execution
options.body: Allow matched shell-shaped commands to run without an enforceable plan, accepting a larger shell-resolution security risk.

recommendation.title: Fix enforceable Darwin shapes
recommendation.body: Implement safe plan construction for deterministic tilde and simple shell-shaped commands, keep prompt behavior for genuinely unenforceable plans, and add focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The current plan-miss gate and recent exec approval refactors are primarily in code authored or recently maintained by vincentkoc.
